questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following spectral lines for atomic hydrogen: A. First line of Paschen series; B. Second line of Balmer series; C. Third line of Paschen series; D. Fourth line of Bracket series. The correct arrangement of the above lines in ascending order of energy is:
questions.solution: Using deltaE=13.6*Z^2*(1/n1^2-1/n2^2) with (A) n1=3,n2=4; (B) n1=2,n2=4; (C) n1=3,n2=6; (D) n1=4,n2=8, the ascending order of energy is D < A < C < B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match List-I (Pair of Compounds) with List-II (Type of Isomers): A. 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene; B. Cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene; C. 2-Butanol and diethyl ether; D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene. List-II: I. Stereoisomers, II. Position isomers, III. Chain isomers, IV. Functional group isomers.
questions.solution: A: 2-methylpropene & but-1-ene are chain isomers (III). B: cis/trans-but-2-ene are stereoisomers (I). C: 2-butanol & diethyl ether are functional isomers (IV). D: but-1-ene & but-2-ene are position isomers (II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Nitrobenzene undergoes the sequence: (1) Br2/FeBr3/heat, (2) Sn/HCl/heat, (3) pH neutralisation, (4) Br2/H2O, (5) NaNO2/HBr 0-5degC, (6) CuBr/NaBr, to give major product (P). The number of bromine atoms in the final product (P) will be:
questions.solution: Bromination of nitrobenzene, reduction to amine, tribromination via Br2/H2O (2,4,6-tribromoaniline), diazotization and Sandmeyer with CuBr replaces NH2 by Br, giving pentabromobenzene: 5 Br atoms in product P.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aqueous HCl reacts with MnO2(s) to form MnCl2(aq), Cl2(g) and H2O(l). What is the weight (in g) of Cl2 liberated when 8.7 g of MnO2(s) is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution? (Mn=55, Cl=35.5, O=16, H=1)
questions.solution: MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O. Moles of MnO2 = 8.7/87 = 0.1 mol, giving 0.1 mol Cl2. Weight = 0.1*71 = 7.1 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: By usual analysis, 1.00 g of compound (X) gave 1.79 g of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound (X) is (nearest integer): (O=16, Mg=24, P=31)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given: Delta_fH(methane,g) = -X kJ/mol; enthalpy of sublimation of graphite = Y kJ/mol; dissociation enthalpy of H2 = Z kJ/mol. The bond enthalpy of C-H bond is given by:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match List-I (Reagents) with List-II (Reaction Name involving aldehydes): A. H2, Pd-BaSO4; B. SnCl2,HCl; C. CrO2Cl2,CS2; D. CO,HCl/Anhyd. AlCl3. List-II: I. Etard Reaction, II. Rosenmund Reduction, III. Gatterman-Koch Reaction, IV. Stephen Reaction.
questions.solution: A. H2/Pd-BaSO4 -> Rosenmund Reduction (II). B. SnCl2/HCl -> Stephen Reaction (IV). C. CrO2Cl2/CS2 -> Etard Reaction (I). D. CO/HCl/AlCl3 -> Gatterman-Koch Reaction (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at T(K): A(g) -> B(g)+C(g). In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar A(g) is allowed to decompose at T(K). After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant (in min^-1) of the reaction? (log2=0.3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of reactivity of the following benzyl halides towards reaction with KCN is: (a) 4-hydroxybenzyl bromide, (b) 4-aminobenzyl bromide, (c) 4-nitrobenzyl bromide, (d) 3-nitrobenzyl bromide
questions.solution: This is an SN1 reaction; rate proportional to carbocation stability, which depends on the electron-donating/withdrawing nature and position of substituents. Order: b>a>d>c.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is Al > Mg > Mg2+ > Al3+. Statement II: The correct order in terms of magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is Cl > Br > S > O. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: Correct order of atomic/ionic size is Mg > Al > Mg2+ > Al3+ (Statement I false, since it says Al>Mg which is wrong). Electron gain enthalpy: Cl has highest magnitude among halogens/chalcogens listed, correct order Cl>Br>S>O (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct statements are: A. Activation energy for enzyme catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is lower than that of acid catalysed hydrolysis. B. During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures of a protein are destroyed but primary structure remains intact. C. Nucleotides are joined together by glycosidic linkage between C1 and C4 carbons of the pentose sugar. D. Quaternary structure of proteins represents overall folding of the polypeptide chain. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: A and B are correct as stated (enzyme catalysis lowers activation energy; denaturation destroys secondary/tertiary but not primary structure). C and D are incorrect statements (nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester linkages, not C1-C4 glycosidic; quaternary structure refers to assembly of multiple polypeptide subunits, not overall folding of a single chain).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of the rate of reaction CH3Br + Nu- -> CH3Nu + Br- with respect to nucleophiles is:
questions.solution: Stability order of anion: ClO4- > CH3COO- > PhO- > OH-. Nucleophilicity is reverse of anion stability: OH- > PhO- > CH3COO- > ClO4-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: CFSE of [Cr(H2O)6]2+ is greater than that of [Mn(H2O)6]2+. Statement II: Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: [Mn(H2O)6]2+ has d5 (WFL) config, CFSE=0. [Cr(H2O)6]2+ has d4 (WFL), CFSE=-0.6*Delta0 (nonzero, greater magnitude), so Statement I is true. K3[Fe(CN)6] (d5, 1 unpaired e-, mu=sqrt(3) BM) vs Na4[Fe(CN)6] (d6, 0 unpaired e-, mu=0), so Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct increasing order of C-H (A), C-O (B), C=O (C) and C≡N (D) bond lengths is:
questions.solution: Approximate bond lengths: C-H (A) ~107pm, C≡N (D) ~116pm, C=O (C) ~121pm, C-O (B) ~143pm. Increasing order: A < D < C < B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given four compounds: (a) n-propyl chloride, (b) iso-propyl chloride, (c) sec-butyl chloride, (d) neo-pentyl chloride. Percentage of carbon in the one which exhibits optical isomerism is:
questions.solution: sec-Butyl chloride (2-chlorobutane) is the chiral molecule (optically active). Molecular formula C4H9Cl, molar mass = 48+9+35.5 = 92.5. %C = (48/92.5)*100 = 51.89% ~ 52%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given below are statements about Mn and Mn2O7: A. Mn forms the oxide Mn2O7 in which Mn is in its highest oxidation state. B. Oxygen stabilizes Mn in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds with Mn. C. Mn2O7 is an ionic oxide. D. The structure of Mn2O7 consists of one bridged oxygen. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: Mn2O7 has Mn in +7 (highest) oxidation state (A true). Oxygen forms multiple (pi) bonds stabilizing high oxidation state Mn (B true). Mn2O7 is a covalent (not ionic) oxide, so C is false. The structure has one bridging oxygen linking two MnO3 tetrahedra (D true).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a closed circuit Daniell cell, which of the following plots (E_cell vs time) is accurate at a given temperature?
questions.solution: The standard E_cell (E°cell) remains constant with time regardless of the cell's operation, as it is defined at standard conditions - hence a horizontal constant line.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: Compound (X) - a bromophenyl ketone attached to a cyclopentane ring bearing a COOH group - dissolves in NaHCO3 solution and has two chiral carbon atoms. Statement II: Compound (Y), CH2=C=C=O type structure, has two carbons with sp3 hybridization, one carbon with sp2 and one carbon with sp hybridization. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: Compound X has two chiral centers on the cyclopentane ring and dissolves in NaHCO3 due to the -COOH group (Statement I true). Compound Y's cumulated diene/ketene-type structure has the described hybridization pattern (sp3, sp3, sp2, sp) as shown (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: The correct order in terms of bond dissociation enthalpy is Cl2 > Br2 > F2 > I2. Statement II: The correct trend in covalent character of metal halides is [SnCl4 > SnCl2], [PbCl4 > PbCl2] and [UF4 > UF6]. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: Bond dissociation enthalpy order Cl2>Br2>F2>I2 is correct (Statement I true). By Fajan's rule, higher charge on cation gives greater covalent character: PbCl4>PbCl2, UF6>UF4 (not UF4>UF6 as stated), SnCl4>SnCl2. So Statement II is false (UF4>UF6 part is wrong).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: On heating a mixture of common salt and K2Cr2O7 in equal amounts along with concentrated H2SO4 in a test tube, a gas is evolved. Formula of the gas evolved and oxidation state of the central metal atom in the gas respectively are:
questions.solution: 4NaCl + K2Cr2O7 + 6H2SO4 -> 2KHSO4 + 2CrO2Cl2 + 4NaHSO4 + 3H2O (chromyl chloride test). In CrO2Cl2, Cr is in +6 oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The first and second ionization constants of H2X are 2.5x10^-8 and 1.0x10^-13 respectively. The concentration of X2- in 0.1M H2X solution is ____ x10^-15 M. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: Since Ka1 >> Ka2, approximate x>>y where x+y~x, x-y~x for the second equilibrium. This gives y ~ Ka2 = 10^-13 M = 100x10^-15 M for [X2-].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The osmotic pressure of a living cell is 12 atm at 300 K. The strength of sodium chloride solution that is isotonic with the living cell at this temperature is ____ gL^-1. (Nearest integer) (R=0.08 L atm K^-1 mol^-1; assume complete dissociation of NaCl; Na=23, Cl=35.5 g/mol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A substance X (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of solvent Y (molar mass=300 g/mol) led to an elevation of the boiling point by 0.5 K. The relative lowering of vapour pressure of solvent Y is ____ x10^-2. (Kb of solvent = 5.0 K kg/mol; nearest integer; assume dilute solution, no association/dissociation)
questions.solution: DeltaTb = i*Kb*m: 0.5 = i*m*5 => i*m=0.1, i*a=15/1000 (a=moles of solute). Relative lowering = i*X_solute = i*a/(a+150/300) = (15/1000)/(1/2) = 3x10^-2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the metal ions among Co2+, Ni2+, Fe2+, V3+ and Ti2+ having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than 3.0 BM. The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is ____.
questions.solution: V3+=3d2, Ti2+=3d2, Ni2+=3d8, Fe2+=3d6, Co2+=3d7. Only Fe2+ (4 unpaired e-, mu>3) and Co2+ (3 unpaired e-, mu>3) exceed 3.0 BM. Sum of unpaired electrons = 4+3 = 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: MX is a sparingly soluble salt following MX(s) <=> M+(aq) + X-(aq); Ksp=10^-10 at 298K. If the standard reduction potential for M+(aq) + e- -> M(s) is E°(M+/M) = 0.79 V, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode E°(X-/MX(s)/M) is ____ mV. (Nearest integer) (2.303RT/F = 0.059 V)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following reactions: PbCl2 + K2CrO4 -> A + 2KCl (hot solution). A + NaOH <=> B + Na2CrO4. PbSO4 + 4CH3COONH4 -> (NH4)2SO4 + X. In the above reactions, A, B and X are respectively.
questions.solution: PbCl2+K2CrO4 -> PbCrO4 (A) + 2KCl. PbCrO4 + 4NaOH(excess) -> Na2[Pb(OH)4] (B) + Na2CrO4. PbSO4+4CH3COONH4 -> (NH4)2[Pb(CH3COO)4] (X) + (NH4)2SO4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct trend for the mentioned property? A. F>P>S>B - First Ionization Energy; B. Cl>F>S>P - Electron Affinity; C. K>Al>Mg>B - Metallic character; D. K2O>Na2O>MgO>Al2O3 - Basic character. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: A: correct IE order F>P>S>B. B: correct EA order Cl>F>S>P (halogens higher than corresponding period chalcogen/pnictogen). C: metallic character order should be K>Mg>Al>B, not K>Al>Mg>B, so C is incorrect. D: correct basic character order K2O>Na2O>MgO>Al2O3. So A, B, D only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify A in the reaction: A --(2H2/Pt)--> decahydronaphthalene; A --(KMnO4)--> cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid + oxalic acid (COOH-COOH).
questions.solution: A is 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene (tetralin), which on hydrogenation with 2H2/Pt gives decahydronaphthalene (decalin), and on oxidative cleavage with KMnO4 gives cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid from the saturated ring plus oxalic acid from the aromatic ring carbons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A hydrocarbon 'P' (C4H8) on reaction with HCl gives an optically active compound 'Q' (C4H9Cl) which on reaction with one mole of ammonia gives compound 'R' (C4H11N). 'R' on diazotization followed by hydrolysis gives 'S'. Identify P, Q, R and S.

options.1: P=but-1-ene; Q=1-chlorobutane derivative; R=amine; S=alcohol (as specifically drawn)
options.2: P=methylenecyclopropane type; Q, R, S as drawn

questions.solution: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 (but-2-ene, P) + HCl -> CH3-CH2-CHCl-CH3 (2-chlorobutane, Q, optically active). Q + NH3 -> CH3-CH2-CH(NH2)-CH3 (R). R diazotization/hydrolysis (NaNO2/HCl) -> CH3-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3 (S, 2-butanol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: The number of pairs among [SiO2,CO2], [SnO,SnO2], [PbO,PbO2] and [GeO,GeO2], which contain oxides that are both amphoteric, is 2. Statement II: BF3 is an electron deficient molecule that can act as a Lewis acid, forms adduct with NH3, and has a trigonal planar geometry. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: SiO2, CO2, GeO, GeO2 are acidic in nature; SnO, SnO2, PbO, PbO2 are amphoteric in nature. So 2 pairs ([SnO,SnO2] and [PbO,PbO2]) are both amphoteric (Statement I true). BF3 is an electron-deficient Lewis acid with sp2 hybridization, trigonal planar geometry, and accepts a lone pair from NH3 to form an adduct (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273K occupy 224 mL. When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL. The formula of the hydrocarbon is:
questions.solution: CxHy + (x+y/4)O2 -> xCO2 + (y/2)H2O(l). Using volume balance: 264 - 80(x+y/4) + 80x = 224 gives y=2. Using the KOH absorption (CO2 absorbed): 264-80(x+1/2)=64 gives x=2. So hydrocarbon is C2H2 (acetylene).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 14.0 g of calcium metal is allowed to react with excess HCl at 1.0 atm pressure and 273 K. Which of the following statements is incorrect? (Ca=40, Cl=35.5, H=1)

options.1: 0.35 mol of H2 gas is evolved
options.2: 7.84 L of H2 gas is evolved
options.4: The limiting reagent is calcium metal

questions.solution: Ca + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2. Moles of Ca = 14/40 = 0.35 mol, giving 0.35 mol H2 (volume=0.35*22.4=7.84L) and 0.35 mol CaCl2 (weight=0.35*111=38.85 g, not 33.3 g). So statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In Carius method, 0.75 g of an organic compound gave 1.2 g of barium sulphate; find percentage of sulphur (molar mass 32 g/mol). Molar mass of barium sulphate is 233 g/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Elements P and Q form two types of non-volatile, non-ionizable compounds PQ and PQ2. When 1g of PQ is dissolved in 50g of solvent 'A', deltaTb was 1.176K, while when 1g of PQ2 is dissolved in 50g of solvent 'A', deltaTb was 0.689K. (Kb of A = 5 K.kg/mol). The molar masses of elements P and Q (in g/mol) respectively, are:
questions.solution: For PQ: 1.176 = 5*(1/M1)*(1000/50), giving M1 (molar mass of PQ) = 85.03. For PQ2: 0.689 = 5*(1/M2)*(1000/50), giving M2 (molar mass of PQ2) = 145.13. Solving Mp+Mq=85.03 and Mp+2Mq=145.13 gives Mq=60.1~60, Mp=24.93~25.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An organic compound (P) on treatment with aqueous ammonia under hot conditions forms compound (Q), which on heating with Br2 and KOH forms compound (R) having molecular formula C6H7N. Names of P, Q and R respectively are:
questions.solution: PhCOOH (benzoic acid, P) + NH3/heat -> PhCONH2 (benzamide, Q). Q + Br2/KOH (Hofmann bromamide degradation) -> PhNH2 (aniline, R, C6H7N).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An organic compound P of molecular formula C6H12O3 gives a positive iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. When P is treated with dilute acid, it produces Q. Q gives a positive Tollen's test and also iodoform test. The structure of P is:

options.1: CH3-C(=O)-CH-CH2(OCH3)(OCH3) type dimethyl acetal at alpha carbon
options.2: CH3-C(=O)-CH2-CH(OCH3)-OCH3 (dimethyl acetal of an aldehyde attached to methyl ketone chain)

questions.solution: P is a methyl ketone with a dimethyl acetal group elsewhere in the chain: the methyl ketone (CH3-CO-) gives positive iodoform but the acetal-protected aldehyde gives negative Tollen's test. On hydrolysis with dilute acid (H2O/H+), the acetal is converted back to the aldehyde (Q), which now gives positive Tollen's test (aldehyde) as well as positive iodoform test (since the methyl ketone portion remains).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: From the following resonance structures of an allyl-nitro type system, the least stable structure is: (structures differing in placement of + and - charges on the conjugated chain and nitro group)
questions.solution: The structure with positive charges on two adjacent atoms is least stable due to charge-charge repulsion between like charges in close proximity, making structure (3) the least stable resonance form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: MnO4(2-), in acidic medium, disproportionates to:
questions.solution: 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ -> 2MnO4^- + MnO2 + 2H2O. Manganate ion disproportionates into permanganate (MnO4-) and manganese dioxide (MnO2) in acidic medium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: The number of species among SF4, NH4+, [NiCl4]2-, XeF4, [PtCl4]2-, SeF4 and [Ni(CN)4]2- that have tetrahedral geometry is 3. Statement II: In the set [NO2, BeH2, BF3, AlCl3], all the molecules have incomplete octet around the central atom. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: Geometries: SF4 (see-saw), XeF4 (square planar), [PtCl4]2- (square planar), [NiCl4]2- (tetrahedral), [Ni(CN)4]2- (square planar), SeF4 (see-saw), NH4+ (tetrahedral). Only 2 species (NiCl4^2- and NH4+) are tetrahedral, not 3, so Statement I is false. NO2 has 7 electrons around N (odd electron species), BeH2 has 4 electrons on Be, BF3 has 6 electrons on B, AlCl3 has 6 electrons on Al - all incomplete octets, so Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: Among [Cu(NH3)4]2+, [Ni(en)3]2+, [Ni(NH3)6]2+ and [Mn(H2O)6]2+, [Mn(H2O)6]2+ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons. Statement II: The number of pairs among {[NiCl4]2-,[Ni(CO)4]}, {[NiCl4]2-,[Ni(CN)4]2-} and {[Ni(CO)4],[Ni(CN)4]2-} that contain only diamagnetic species is two. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: [Cu(NH3)4]2+ (d9, dsp2) has 1 unpaired electron. [Ni(en)3]2+ (d8, sp3d2) has 2 unpaired electrons. [Ni(NH3)6]2+ (d8, sp3d2) has 2 unpaired electrons. [Mn(H2O)6]2+ (d5, sp3d2) has 5 unpaired electrons (maximum), so Statement I is true. [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic, [NiCl4]2- is paramagnetic, [Ni(CN)4]2- is diamagnetic. Only the pair {[Ni(CO)4],[Ni(CN)4]2-} has both diamagnetic, so only 1 pair qualifies (not two), making Statement II false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the correct statement(s) from the following: A. Propanal and propanone are functional isomers. B. Ethoxyethane and methoxypropane are metamers. C. But-2-ene shows optical isomerism. D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene are functional isomers. E. Pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are chain isomers. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: A: propanal and propanone are functional isomers (true). B: ethoxyethane and methoxypropane are metamers (true, both ethers with different alkyl groups on either side of O). C: but-2-ene does NOT have optical isomerism (false - it lacks a chiral center). D: but-1-ene and but-2-ene are positional isomers, not functional isomers (false). E: pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are chain isomers (true). So A, B, E only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the correct statements: A. Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids. B. Histidine does not contain a heterocyclic ring in its structure. C. Proline is a six-membered cyclic ring amino acid. D. Glycine does not have a chiral centre. E. Cysteine has characteristic feature of side chain as MeS-CH2-CH2-. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: A: Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids (true). B: Histidine DOES contain a heterocyclic (imidazole) ring, so B is false. C: Proline is a FIVE-membered cyclic ring amino acid, not six-membered, so C is false. D: Glycine (simplest amino acid, R=H) does not have a chiral centre (true). E: Cysteine's characteristic side chain is -CH2-SH, not MeS-CH2-CH2- (that describes methionine), so E is false. So A and D only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following graphs between pressure 'P' versus volume 'V' represents the maximum work done? (Four P-V diagrams shown with different paths between states at 22.4L and 44.8L, pressures 1.0 and 2.0 bar)
questions.solution: The area under the P-V curve equals the magnitude of work done. In the option with a single smooth reversible expansion curve from (22.4L, 2.0 bar) to (44.8L, 1.0 bar), the enclosed area (and hence magnitude of work) is maximum compared to the cyclic paths (where net work is smaller due to path retracing) or the isochoric option (zero net work).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction N2O4 <=> 2NO2, a graph of G (kJ/mol) vs fraction of N2O4 dissociated is plotted (constant P,T), with values 5.40 and 0.84 kJ marked. Identify correct statements: A. Standard free energy change for the reaction is -5.40 kJ/mol. B. As deltaG(standard) in graph is positive, N2O4 will not dissociate into NO2 at all. C. Reverse reaction will go to completion. D. When 1 mole of N2O4 changes into equilibrium mixture, value of deltaG(standard) = -0.84 kJ/mol. E. When 2 mole of NO2 changes into equilibrium mixture, deltaG(standard) for equilibrium mixture is -6.24 kJ/mol.
questions.solution: From the graph, delta_r*G° = G°B - G°A = +5.40 kJ/mol (positive, not -5.40), so A is false. Since delta_r*G°=+ve, N2O4 will PARTIALLY dissociate (equilibrium exists, doesn't mean zero dissociation), so B is false. The reverse reaction reaches equilibrium at point E (partially completed, not complete), so C is false. For 1 mole N2O4 forming the equilibrium mixture, delta_r*G° = -0.84 kJ/mol (true, D). For 2 mole NO2 forming equilibrium mixture, deltaG° = -5.4-0.84 = -6.24 kJ/mol (true, E). So D and E only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Statement I: When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies. Statement II: The frequency of the second line of the Balmer series obtained from He+ is equal to that of the first line of the Lyman series obtained from a hydrogen atom. Choose the correct answer:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: Statement I describes the standard mechanism of atomic hydrogen emission spectra (true). For Statement II: 1st Lyman line of H: 1/lambda = R(1)^2(1/1^2-1/2^2) = 3R/4. 2nd Balmer line of He+ (Z=2): 1/lambda' = R(2)^2(1/2^2-1/4^2) = 3R/4. Since 1/lambda=1/lambda', the frequencies are equal (true).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of the same order are identical. Let the activation energy of the first reaction exceed the activation energy of the second reaction by 20 kJ/mol. If k1 and k2 are the rate constants of the first and second reaction respectively at 300K, then ln(k2/k1) will be (nearest integer). (R=8.3 J K^-1 mol^-1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pH and conductance of a weak acid (HX) was found to be 5 and 4x10^-5 S respectively. The conductance was measured under standard conditions using a cell where the electrode plates having a surface area of 1 cm^2 were at a distance of 1.5 cm apart. The value of the limiting molar conductivity is ____ Sm^2 mol^-1 (nearest integer). (degree of dissociation << 1)
questions.solution: [H+]=10^-5=[HX]*alpha=[HX]*(Lambda_m/Lambda_m_infinity). Cell constant K=G* = 1.5/1=1.5 cm^-1 (given as 15/1 in some steps, using given values k=G.G*=4x10^-5*15=6x10^-4 S/cm). Lambda_m = k*1000/[HX]. Substituting into [H+] equation and solving gives Lambda_m_infinity = 60000 S.cm^2/mol = 6 S.m^2/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Using thermodynamic data for substances AB(g), A2(g), B2(g) at 500K (given DeltaHf and S values), one mole each of A2(g) and B2(g) are taken in a 1L closed flask and allowed to establish equilibrium at 500K: A2(g)+B2(g) <=> 2AB(g). The value of x (DeltaHf of B2 in kJ/mol) is ____ (nearest integer). (log K = 2.2, R=8.3 J K^-1 mol^-1)
questions.solution: DeltaH° = 2*32-(6+x) = (58-x) kJ. DeltaS° = 2*222-(146+280) = 18 J/K. DeltaG° = -RTlnK = -(8.314*500*2.2*2.303)/1000 = -21.06 kJ. Using DeltaG°=DeltaH°-T*DeltaS°: 58-x-500*(18/1000) = -21.06, solving gives x = 70.06, i.e., 70 (nearest integer).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider a reaction sequence starting from benzene: conc.HNO3+conc.H2SO4 (333K) -> P; then (1) Sn/HCl/heat (2) pH neutralised -> Q; then (CH3CO)2O -> R; then conc.HNO3+conc.H2SO4 -> S (major product); then (1) HCl/EtOH/heat (2) pH neutralised -> T. The percentage of nitrogen in product T formed is ____ % (nearest integer). (H:1, C:12, N:14, O:16)
questions.solution: Benzene -> nitrobenzene (P) -> aniline (Q, via Sn/HCl reduction) -> acetanilide (R, via acetylation) -> nitration gives p-nitroacetanilide (S, major product due to directing effect of acetamido group) -> hydrolysis (HCl/EtOH) gives p-nitroaniline (T). Molecular formula of T (C6H6N2O2): mol wt = 6*12+6*1+2*14+2*16 = 138. %N = (28/138)*100 = 20.29% ~ 20%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following reactions: NaCl+K2Cr2O7+H2SO4 -> A+KHSO4+NaHSO4+H2O. A+NaOH -> B+NaCl+H2O. B+H2SO4+H2O2 -> C+Na2SO4+H2O. In product C, X is the number of O2(2-) (peroxide) units, Y is the total number of oxygen atoms present, and Z is the oxidation state of Cr. The value of X+Y+Z is ____.
questions.solution: A = CrO2Cl2 (chromyl chloride). B = Na2CrO4 (sodium chromate). C = CrO5 (chromium peroxide, blue peroxide, with structure containing two peroxide (-O-O-) groups and one =O group around Cr in +6 oxidation state). X=2 (peroxide units), Y=5 (total oxygen atoms: 2 peroxide groups=4 O + 1 double-bond O = 5), Z=6 (oxidation state of Cr). X+Y+Z = 2+5+6 = 13.

questions.question: At T(K), 100 g of 98% H2SO4 (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of 49% H2SO4 (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of H2SO4 in the resultant solution? (H=1u, S=32u, O=16u)
A dibromo compound (structure shown) reacts with 2NaNH2 to give X; X is further treated with NaNH2 then an alkyl bromide to give Y. The product Y formed is:
questions.solution: Vicinal dibromide undergoes double dehydrohalogenation (E2) to form terminal alkyne, then SN2 alkylation with isopropyl bromide gives 2-methylhex-3-yne.

questions.question: A + 2B → AB2. 36.0 g of A (molar mass 60 g/mol) and 56.0 g of B (molar mass 80 g/mol) are allowed to react. Which statements are correct? (A) A is limiting reagent (B) 77.0 g of AB2 is formed (C) Molar mass of AB2 is 140 g/mol (D) 15.0 g of A is left unreacted.
questions.solution: Moles: A=0.6, B=0.7. B is limiting reagent (0.35 mol AB2 needs 0.35 mol A but only 0.35 available exactly using B). Molar mass of AB2=220 g/mol. Mass of AB2 formed = 0.35×220=77g (B correct). A remaining = 0.25×60=15g (D correct).

questions.question: Statement I: The first ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn. Statement II: The second and third ionization enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn.
questions.solution: Cr=[Ar]3d⁵4s¹, Mn=[Ar]3d⁵4s². IE1(Cr)<IE1(Mn) (Statement I true, due to stable half-filled configuration in Mn's removal difficulty is different — actually IE1(Cr)<IE1(Mn)). IE2(Cr)>IE2(Mn) but IE3(Cr)<IE3(Mn), so Statement II is false.

questions.question: Cyclohexylamine reacts with C6H5COCl/NaOH to give [A], which on treatment with LiAlH4/H2O gives [B]. The final product [B] is:
questions.solution: Benzoylation gives the amide [A]; LiAlH4 reduction of the amide C=O to CH2 gives the secondary amine [B], cyclohexyl-NH-CH2-C6H5.

questions.question: When 1 g of compound (X) is subjected to Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, 15 mL of 1M H2SO4 was neutralized by ammonia evolved. The percentage of nitrogen in compound (X) is:

Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation: (A) Factor e^(-Ea/RT) corresponds to fraction of molecules with KE less than Ea. (B) At given T, lower Ea means faster reaction. (C) 10°C rise generally doubles reaction rate. (D) Plot of logk vs 1/T gives straight line with slope -Ea/R.
questions.solution: Fact based: statement B and C are standard true statements about the Arrhenius equation and rate-temperature relationship.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of the given ester (propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate structure) is:
questions.solution: Numbering the 7-carbon acid chain with bromo at C2 and methyl at C5, esterified with propyl alcohol gives propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate.

questions.question: Statement I: Among N, As, Sb, P — X (most electronegative) and Y (least electronegative); oxides X2O3 and Y2O3 are acidic and amphoteric respectively. Statement II: BCl3 is covalent, hydrolyses in water to give [B(OH)4]⁻ and [B(H2O)6]³⁺.
questions.solution: X=N, Y=Sb: N2O3 acidic, Sb2O3 amphoteric — Statement I true. BCl3 hydrolyses to B(OH)3 + 3HCl, not the ionic species stated — Statement II false.

questions.question: Match List-I (Reaction of glucose with) with List-II (Product formed): A. Hydroxylamine, B. Br2 water, C. Excess acetic anhydride, D. Concentrated HNO3 — with I. Gluconic acid, II. Glucose pentaacetate, III. Saccharic acid, IV. Glucoxime.
questions.solution: Glucose + NH2OH → Glucoxime (A-IV); Glucose + Br2/H2O → Gluconic acid (B-I); Glucose + excess (CH3CO)2O → Glucose pentaacetate (C-II); Glucose + conc. HNO3 → Saccharic acid (D-III).

questions.question: Among H2S, H2O, NF3, NH3 and CHCl3, identify the molecule (X) with lowest dipole moment value. The number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central atom of molecule (X) is:
questions.solution: NF3 has the lowest dipole moment (0.23 D) among the given molecules due to opposing bond and lone pair dipole contributions. Central N atom has 1 lone pair.

questions.question: Statement I: C<O<N<F is the correct order of first ionization enthalpy values. Statement II: S>Se>Te>Po>O is the correct order of magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values.
questions.solution: IE order C<O<N<F is correct (O is anomalously lower than N due to stable half-filled 2p³). Electron gain enthalpy magnitude order S>Se>Te>Po>O (~200,195,190,174,141 kJ/mol) is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following mixtures gives a buffer solution with pH=9.25? Given pKb(NH4OH)=4.75.
questions.solution: pOH=pKb+log(salt/base). For pH=9.25 (pOH=4.75), salt=base is required, i.e. equal millimoles of NH4OH and NH4Cl formed. Option 2 gives 100 mmol NH4OH reacting with 50 mmol HCl leaving 50 mmol NH4OH and forming 50 mmol NH4Cl — equal amounts, satisfying the condition.

questions.question: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is x J. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is:
questions.solution: Using Rydberg formula for n=2→3 (x) and n=2→4 transitions, ratio ΔE/x = 27/20 = 1.35 ⇒ ΔE = 1.35x.

questions.question: Identify the correct statements: A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard. B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air. C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric. D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water. E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass.
options: A, B, C and E only
questions.solution: A primary standard must be soluble in water (to prepare standard solutions), so D is incorrect; high (not low) molar mass is generally preferred to reduce weighing error, so E is incorrect. A, B, C are correct.

questions.question: [Ni(PPh3)2Cl2] is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements: A. Exhibits geometrical isomerism. B. Complex is white in colour. C. Calculated spin-only magnetic moment is 2.84 BM. D. Calculated CFSE of Ni is -0.8Δ0. E. Geometrical arrangement of ligands is similar to that in Ni(CO)4.
questions.solution: Being paramagnetic, the complex is tetrahedral (Ni²⁺, d⁸). Tetrahedral complexes do not show geometrical isomerism (A incorrect). The complex is blue, not white (B incorrect). CFSE = -0.8Δt (not Δ0), so labeling it Δ0 is incorrect (D incorrect). C (2.84 BM) and E (tetrahedral like Ni(CO)4) are correct.

questions.question: Consider the reduction processes: Al³⁺+3e⁻→Al(s), E°=-1.66V; Fe³⁺+e⁻→Fe²⁺, E°=+0.77V; Co³⁺+e⁻→Co²⁺, E°=+1.81V; Cr³⁺+3e⁻→Cr(s), E°=-0.74V. The tendency to act as reducing agent decreases in the order:
questions.solution: Reducing power is inversely proportional to reduction potential; ordering E° from most negative to most positive gives Al>Cr>Fe²⁺>Co²⁺ as reducing agent strength.

questions.question: The compound A, C8H8O2 reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as:
questions.solution: A is p-anisaldehyde (4-methoxybenzaldehyde, C8H8O2) which lacks α-hydrogens, undergoes crossed Aldol with acetophenone (single product), and undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH to give 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol and the corresponding carboxylate.

questions.question: 3,3-Dimethyl-2-butanol cannot be prepared by which of the routes (A: Grignard on pivaldehyde; B: acid-catalyzed hydration of an alkene; C: ozonolysis/reduction sequence; D: LiAlH4 reduction of ketone; E: acid-catalyzed hydration of alkyne)?
questions.solution: Route B (acid-catalyzed hydration of the alkene) proceeds via carbocation with an ethyl/methyl shift giving a rearranged tertiary alcohol, not the target. Route E (Markovnikov hydration of the alkyne via HgSO4) gives a methyl ketone (pinacolone), not the alcohol. Routes A, C, D correctly give 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol.

questions.question: The dibromo compound [P] (molecular formula C9H10Br2) when heated with excess sodamide followed by treatment with dilute HCl gives [Q]. On warming [Q] with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid yields [R] which gives positive iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. The compound [P] is:
options: Structure 3 (gem-dibromide on benzylic tertiary carbon of p-cresol derivative)
questions.solution: P is a gem-dibromide (ArCBr2CH3 type, on a p-tolyl ring) that upon double dehydrohalogenation with NaNH2 forms terminal alkyne Q (Ar-C≡CH); acid-catalyzed hydration (HgSO4/H2SO4) gives methyl ketone R (Ar-CO-CH3), which is iodoform positive and Tollens negative.

questions.question: Consider the transition metal ions Mn3+, Cr3+, Fe3+ and Co3+, all forming low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals is
questions.solution: Co3+ (3d6, low spin): t2g^6 eg^0, unpaired=0. Fe3+ (3d5): t2g^5, unpaired=1. Cr3+ (3d3): t2g^3, unpaired=3. Mn3+ (3d4): t2g^4, unpaired=2. Order: Cr3+(3) > Mn3+(2) > Fe3+(1) > Co3+(0).

questions.question: The formal charges on the atoms marked (1) to (4) in the Lewis representation of HNO3 molecule are respectively
questions.solution: For HNO3 Lewis structure: the singly-bonded O attached to H has formal charge 0, the central N has formal charge +1, the doubly bonded O has formal charge 0, and the O- (single bond, three lone pairs) has formal charge -1.

questions.question: Statement I: Phenol on treatment with CHCl3/aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification produces p-hydroxybenzaldehyde as major product and o-hydroxybenzaldehyde as minor product. Statement II: The mixture of p-hydroxybenzaldehyde and o-hydroxybenzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation.
questions.answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction on phenol, o-hydroxybenzaldehyde is actually the major product (due to intramolecular H-bonding stabilizing it) while p-hydroxybenzaldehyde is minor, making Statement I false. The o-isomer, being intramolecularly H-bonded and more volatile, can be separated by steam distillation, making Statement II true.

questions.question: The energy required by electrons present in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom to be excited to the second Bohr orbit is ____ J mol^-1. (Given RH = 2.18×10^-11 ergs)

A p-block element (E) and hydrogen form a binary cation (EHx)+, while EH3 on treatment with K2HgI4 in alkaline medium gives a precipitate of basic mercury(II) amido-iodide. Identify the correct first ionisation enthalpy value for element E.
questions.solution: Element E is Nitrogen (Nessler's reagent test confirms NH3, and NH4+ is the binary cation). Among B, C, N, O, nitrogen has the highest first ionization energy due to its half-filled stability, i.e. 1402 kJ/mol.

questions.question: In the reaction 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2Al3+(aq) + 6Cl-(aq) + 3H2(g), which statement is correct?

options.1: 11.2 L H2 per mole HCl consumed
options.2: 67.2 L H2 per mole Al reacted
options.3: 12 L HCl consumed per 6 L H2 produced
options.4: 33.6 L H2 produced regardless of T,P per mole Al

questions.answer: 11.2 L H2(g) at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed
questions.solution: Moles of H2 produced = (3/6)×moles HCl used = 0.5×moles HCl, so per mole HCl, 0.5 mol H2 = 11.2 L at STP is produced.

questions.question: Consider a solution of CO2(g) dissolved in water in a closed container. Which plot correctly represents variation of log(partial pressure of CO2 in vapour phase) [y-axis] with log(mole fraction of CO2 in water) [x-axis] at 25°C?
questions.answer: Option 3 (straight line through origin with positive slope, log-log plot per Henry's Law)
questions.solution: From Henry's law, P(g) = KH·X(g), so logP(g) = logKH + logX(g), a straight line with slope 1 and positive intercept logKH.

questions.question: A first row transition metal (M) does not liberate H2 gas from dilute HCl. 1 mol of aqueous MSO4 is treated with excess aqueous KCN and then H2S(g) is passed through the solution. The amount of MS (metal sulphide) formed is ____ mol.
questions.solution: M is Cu (does not react with dilute HCl). CuSO4 with excess KCN forms the perfect/stable complex [Cu(CN)4]3-, which does not release Cu2+ ions to react with H2S, so no sulphide precipitate forms.

questions.question: The correct order of reactivity of CH3Br in methanol with the nucleophiles F-, I-, C2H5O- and C6H5O- is
questions.solution: Order of nucleophilicity (SN2 in polar protic solvent): I- > C2H5O- > PhO- > F-, based on polarizability and basicity trends.

questions.question: Match List-I (Thermodynamic Process) with List-II (Magnitude in kJ): A. Reversible isothermal expansion of 2 mol ideal gas from 2dm3 to 20dm3 at 300K. B. Irreversible isothermal expansion of 1 mol ideal gas from 1m3 to 3m3 at 300K against constant pressure 3kPa. C. Change in internal energy for adiabatic expansion of 1 mol ideal gas, ΔT=320K, Cv=3R/2. D. Change in enthalpy at constant pressure, 1 mol ideal gas, ΔT=337K, Cp=5R/2.
questions.solution: A: W=-nRTln(V2/V1)= -11.5 kJ (magnitude II). B: W=-Pext(V2-V1)=-6 kJ (magnitude III). C: ΔU=nCvΔT≈3.99≈4 kJ (magnitude I). D: ΔH=nCpΔT=7 kJ (magnitude IV).

questions.question: Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with CH3COCl/AlCl3 gives a meta-substituted acetophenone product (3-nitroacetophenone). Statement II: NO2 group is m-directing and deactivating.
questions.answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Nitrobenzene, being highly deactivated, does not undergo Friedel-Crafts acylation at all, so Statement I is incorrect. Statement II is a correct general property of the NO2 group.

questions.question: A → products (first order reaction). Run 1: 100 mL of 10M A. Run 2: 200 mL of 10M A. Run 3: 100 mL of 10M A + 100 mL H2O added. The correct variation of rate of reaction is
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, Rate = k[A], depending only on concentration, not volume. Run1 and Run2 have same concentration (10M) so equal rates; Run3 has diluted (lower) concentration, so lower rate.

questions.question: Match List-I (Reagents: NH2-NH2/KOH; Ag(NH3)2OH; Aq. CuSO4+Sodium Potassium tartarate/KOH; Zn-Hg/HCl) with List-II (Reaction names: Tollen's Test; Clemmensen Reduction; Wolff-Kishner Reduction; Fehling's Test).
questions.solution: NH2-NH2/KOH corresponds to Wolff-Kishner Reduction (III). Ag(NH3)2OH corresponds to Tollen's Test (I). Aq. CuSO4 with Rochelle's salt/KOH corresponds to Fehling's Test (IV). Zn-Hg/HCl corresponds to Clemmensen Reduction (II).

questions.question: Statement I: The halogen that makes the longest bond with hydrogen in HX has the smallest covalent radius in its group. Statement II: A group 15 element's hydride EH3 has the lowest boiling point among corresponding hydrides of other group 15 elements; the maximum covalency of that element E is 4.
questions.answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution: Bond length order HF<HCl<HBr<HI, so HI (longest bond) corresponds to Iodine which has the largest, not smallest, covalent radius in its group — Statement I is false. PH3 has the lowest boiling point among group 15 hydrides, and phosphorus's maximum possible covalency is 6, not 4 — Statement II is also false.

questions.question: Statement I: Sucrose is dextrorotatory; hydrolysis gives a mixture showing laevorotation. Statement II: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose; since laevorotation of glucose (fructose, actually) is more than dextrorotation of glucose, resulting solution becomes laevorotatory.
questions.answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Sucrose [α]=+66.5° (dextrorotatory); hydrolysis gives glucose [α]=+52.5° and fructose [α]=-92.4°. Statement I is true (hydrolysed mixture is laevorotatory overall). Statement II incorrectly attributes the laevorotation to glucose instead of fructose's stronger laevorotation, so it's false.

questions.question: 'A' is a neutral organic compound (C8H9ON). On treatment with aqueous Br2/HO-, 'A' forms compound 'B' soluble in dilute acid. 'B' with aqueous NaNO2/HCl (0-5°C) gives 'C', which with CuCN/NaCN gives 'D'. Hydrolysis of 'D' gives 'E' (also obtainable from hydrolysis of 'A'). 'E' with acidified KMnO4 gives 'F' containing two different types of hydrogen atoms. Identify structure of 'A'.
questions.solution: 'A' undergoes Hofmann bromamide degradation (Br2/KOH) on the amide to give the aromatic amine 'B' (p-toluidine), which via diazotization/Sandmeyer (NaNO2/HCl then CuCN) gives the nitrile 'D' (p-tolunitrile), whose hydrolysis gives 'E' (p-toluic acid, also obtainable from hydrolysis of amide 'A'). Oxidation of the methyl group with KMnO4 gives terephthalic acid 'F', which has two distinct types of H (aromatic and COOH). Hence A = p-toluamide.

questions.question: The correct order of rate of reaction of the following reactants with a nucleophile by SN1 mechanism is (I: bromocyclohexane-fused bicyclic bridgehead Br, II: bridgehead Br in bicyclic system, III: tert-butyl bromide, IV: triphenylmethyl bromide - structures I and II are rigid bridgehead systems).
questions.solution: Rate of SN1 ∝ stability of carbocation formed. Structures I and II are bridgehead carbocations, unstable due to Bredt's rule (cannot achieve planarity); I has more +I stabilization than II, but both are less reactive than III (3° carbocation) and IV (highly stabilized triphenylmethyl cation). Order: II < I < III < IV.

questions.question: Two p-block elements X and Y form fluorides of the type EF3. XF3 is a Lewis acid and YF3 is a Lewis base. The hybridization of the central atoms of XF3 and YF3 respectively are
questions.solution: XF3 = BF3 (Lewis acid, sp2 hybridized, electron deficient). YF3 = NF3 (Lewis base, sp3 hybridized, has a lone pair).

questions.question: As compared with chlorocyclohexane, which statements correctly apply to chlorobenzene? A. Negative charge magnitude more on Cl atoms. B. C-Cl bond has partial double bond character. C. C-Cl bond is less polar. D. C-Cl bond is longer due to repulsion between delocalised ring electrons and lone pairs on Cl. E. C-Cl bond formed using sp2 hybridised orbital of carbon.
questions.solution: In chlorobenzene, resonance donation of Cl lone pair into the ring gives the C-Cl bond partial double bond character (B) and makes it less polar than in chlorocyclohexane (C) since -I effect is opposed by +M; the carbon is sp2 hybridized (E). Statement A is false (charge on Cl is actually reduced due to resonance donation) and D is false (bond is shorter, not longer, due to partial double bond character).

questions.question: Statement I: Henry's law constant KH is constant with respect to variations in solution's concentration over the range for which the solution is ideally dilute. Statement II: KH does not differ for the same solute in different solvents.
questions.answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Statement I correctly describes the applicability range of Henry's Law. Statement II is false because KH depends on the nature of both the gas (solute) and the solvent.

questions.question: The cycloalkane (X) on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of (X) and gives product (Y) in which C:Br ratio is 3:1. The percentage of bromine in product (Y) is ____ %. (Nearest integer) (Molar mass: H:1, C:12, O:16, Br:80)
questions.solution: X = C6H10 (cyclohexene), Y = C6H10Br2. Molecular mass of C6H10Br2 = 72+10+160 = 242. % Br = 160/242 ×100 = 66.11% ≈ 66%.

questions.question: Consider the electrochemical cell Pt|HSnO2-(aq)|Sn(OH)6(2-)(aq)|Bi2O3(s)|Bi(s) at 298K. If reaction quotient at a given time is 10^6, the cell EMF (Ecell) is ____ ×10^-1 V (Nearest integer). Given E°(Bi2O3/Bi,OH-) = -0.44V, E°(Sn(OH)6(2-)/HSnO2-,OH-) = -0.90V.
The temperature at which the rate constants of two gaseous reactions become equal is ____ K (nearest integer). X→Y: k1=10^6 e^(-30000/T). P→Q: k2=10^4 e^(-24000/T). Given ln10=2.303.

Sodium fusion extract of an organic compound (Y) with CHCl3 and chlorine water gives violet color to the CHCl3 layer. 0.15 g of (Y) gave 0.12 g of silver halide precipitate in Carius method. Percentage of halogen in compound (Y) is ____ (Nearest integer). (Molar mass: C:12,H:1,Cl:35.5,Br:80,I=127)
questions.solution: Violet color indicates the halogen is Iodine. % of I = (atomic weight of I / molecular weight of AgI) × (mass of AgI/mass of sample) ×100 = (127/235)×(0.12/0.15)×100 = 43.23% ≈ 43%.

questions.question: Dissociation of gas A2 occurs as A2(g) ⇌ 2A(g). At equilibrium, total pressure is 1 bar at 300K. Standard Gibbs energy of formation: A2 = -100.00 kJ/mol, A = -50.832 kJ/mol. The degree of dissociation of A2(g) is given by (x×10^-2)^(1/2) where x = ____ (Nearest integer). [R=8 J/mol.K, log2=0.3010, log3=0.48]
A concentration vs time plot for a dissociation reaction A→nB is given. Based on the data of the initial phase of the reaction (initial 10 min), the value of n is ____.
questions.solution: At t=0, [A]=0.05; at t=10min, [A]=0.04, [B]=0.01×n. Change in A (0.01) relates to B formed (0.03), so 0.01n=0.03, n=3.

questions.question: It is noticed that Pb²⁺ is more stable than Pb⁴⁺ but Sn²⁺ is less stable than Sn⁴⁺. Reactions: PbO2+Pb→2PbO (ΔrG°(1)); SnO2+Sn→2SnO (ΔrG°(2)). Identify the correct set.
questions.solution: Since Pb²⁺ is more stable, reaction 1 is spontaneous (ΔrG°(1)<0). Since Sn²⁺ is less stable, reaction 2 is non-spontaneous (ΔrG°(2)>0).

questions.question: In an electrochemical cell with a metal electrode M undergoing M→M⁺+e, the cation M⁺ is present at two concentrations c1 and c2 separated by a semi-permeable membrane. Which statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential?
options: If c1 is at anode, then c1=c2
If c1 is at cathode, then c1<c2
If c1 is at cathode, then c1>c2
If c1 is at anode, then c1>c2
questions.answer: If c1 is at cathode, then c1>c2
questions.solution: For a concentration cell, positive E_cell requires the cathode to have higher concentration than the anode. If c1 is at cathode, E_cell = -0.059log(c2/c1) > 0 requires c2<c1, i.e., c1>c2.

questions.question: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of
questions.solution: DNA and RNA are chiral due to the chiral 2-deoxy-D-ribose and D-ribose sugar units respectively.

questions.question: Identify the CORRECT set of details: A. [Co(NH3)6]³⁺: Inner orbital complex, d²sp³. B. [MnCl6]³⁻: Outer orbital complex, sp³d². C. [CoF6]³⁻: Outer orbital, d²sp³. D. [FeF6]³⁻: Outer orbital, sp³d². E. [Ni(CN)4]²⁻: Inner orbital, sp³.
questions.solution: Co³⁺ with NH3 (SFL): d²sp³, inner orbital (A correct). Mn³⁺ with Cl⁻ (WFL): sp³d², outer orbital (B correct). Co³⁺ with F⁻ (WFL): sp³d² not d²sp³ (C incorrect as stated). Fe³⁺ with F⁻ (WFL): sp³d², outer orbital (D correct). Ni²⁺ with CN⁻ (SFL): dsp², inner orbital, not sp³ (E incorrect).

questions.question: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of X and phosphorus is higher than that between phosphorus and Y. X & Y are respectively
questions.solution: EN values: N=3.0, P=2.1, As=2.0. |EN(N)-EN(P)|=0.9 > |EN(P)-EN(As)|=0.1, so X=N, Y=As.

questions.question: Statement I: (CH3)3C⁺ is more stable than •CH3⁺ as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in (CH3)3C⁺. Statement II: •CH3⁺ is less stable than (CH3)3C⁺ as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in •CH3⁺.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Statement I is correct due to nine hyperconjugative C-H bonds available. Statement II is false since methyl cation CH3⁺ has no alkyl hydrogens for hyperconjugation (it's a primary carbocation with no adjacent C-H for hyperconjugation in the way described).

questions.question: Iodoform test can differentiate between: A. Methanol and Ethanol. B. CH3COOH and CH3CH2COOH. C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone. D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one. E. Anisole and acetone.
questions.solution: Ethanol gives positive iodoform test (methanol doesn't) - A correct. Acetone gives positive iodoform test (anisole doesn't) - E correct. Acetic acid, cyclohexanone, and pentan-3-one do not give the iodoform test as they lack the CH3-CO- or CH3-CH(OH)- group.

questions.question: Statement I: The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg. Statement II: The ionic radius of O²⁻ is larger than that of F⁻.
options: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Statement I is true but statement II is false
questions.answer: Both statement I and statement II are true
questions.solution: Na⁺ has a stable fully-filled noble gas configuration, so removing a second electron requires much more energy than for Mg⁺ (which still has one electron to lose from a stable config easily) - Statement I true. O²⁻ has a larger ionic radius than F⁻ due to greater electron-electron repulsion for the same number of protons - Statement II true.

questions.question: A dibromocyclopentane derivative undergoes (i) Zn, Δ (ii) HBr to give major product P. Identify (P).
questions.solution: Zn/Δ causes debromination to form a cyclopentene ring fused system; addition of HBr proceeds via the more stable carbocation with a 1,2-hydride shift, giving the rearranged bromide product (structure 2).

questions.question: Reactions at T(K): I. A→products. II. 5Br⁻(aq)+BrO3⁻(aq)+6H⁺(aq)→3Br2(aq)+3H2O(l). Both reactions started at 10:00am; rates are equal at 10:10am. -Δ[Br⁻]/Δt at 10:10am is 2×10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹min⁻¹. Concentration of A at 10:10am is 10⁻² mol L⁻¹. What is the first order rate constant (min⁻¹) of reaction I?
questions.solution: Rate of reaction II = (1/5)(2×10⁻⁴) = 4×10⁻⁵ mol/L/min. Setting this equal to k[A]: 4×10⁻⁵=k×10⁻², k=4×10⁻³ min⁻¹.

questions.question: Which statements are TRUE about the Haloform reaction? A. NaOCl reacts with KI to give KOI. B. KOI is a reducing agent. C. α,β-unsaturated methylketone (CH3-CH=CH-CO-CH3) will give iodoform reaction. D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test. E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
questions.solution: NaOCl+KI→NaCl+KOI (A correct). KOI is an oxidizing agent, not reducing (B incorrect). The α,β-unsaturated methyl ketone still contains the CH3-CO- group and gives iodoform reaction (C correct). Isopropyl alcohol does give a positive iodoform test (D incorrect). Methanoic (formic) acid does not give iodoform test (E incorrect).

questions.question: Which statements are NOT TRUE about XeO2F2? A. It has a see-saw shape. B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell. C. The O-Xe-O bond angle is close to 180°. D. The F-Xe-F bond angle is close to 180°. E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in XeO2F2.
questions.solution: The molecule does have a see-saw shape (A true). Xe actually has 7 electron pairs, not 5 (B false/not true). O-Xe-O bond angle is close to 120°, not 180° (C false/not true). F-Xe-F bond angle is close to 180° (D true). Xe has 14 valence electrons in this molecule, not 16 (E false/not true). So B, C, E are the NOT TRUE statements.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statements: A. Notation ²⁴₁₂Mg represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons. B. Wavelength of radiation of frequency 4.5×10¹⁵ s⁻¹ is 6.7×10⁻⁸ m. C. One radiation has λ1=900nm, energy=E1; another has λ2=300nm, energy=E2, E1:E2=3:1. D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000pm that provides 1J of energy is 1.006×10¹⁶.
questions.solution: ²⁴₁₂Mg has 12 protons and 12 neutrons, not 24 protons (A incorrect). λ=c/v=6.67×10⁻⁸m (B correct). E1/E2=λ2/λ1=300/900=1/3, not 3:1 (C incorrect). Number of photons = Energy/(hc/λ) = 10¹⁶ (D correct, close to stated value).

questions.question: In Carius method 0.2425g of an organic compound gave 0.5253g silver chloride. The percentage of chlorine in the organic compound is

A mixed ether (P), when heated with excess hot concentrated HI produces two different alkyl iodides which when treated with aq. NaOH give compounds (Q) and (R). Both (Q) and (R) give yellow precipitate with NaOI. Identify the mixed ether (P):
questions.solution: Ether cleavage with excess conc. HI gives ethyl iodide and sec-butyl iodide; hydrolysis gives ethanol (Q) and sec-butanol (R), both of which contain the CH3-CH(OH)- pattern and give positive iodoform/NaOI test.

questions.question: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between KI and acidified K2Cr2O7 solution is:
questions.solution: K2Cr2O7 + KI + H⁺ → I2 + Cr³⁺; chromium is reduced from +6 to +3 in the final product.

questions.question: The work functions of two metals (MA and MB) are in 1:2 ratio. When exposed to photons of energy 6eV, the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of MA:MB is in ratio 2.642:1. The work functions (in eV) of MA and MB are respectively.

Statement I: 3,4-diaminotoluene-type diamine can be synthesized from the corresponding diethyl-substituted arene using i) acidic KMnO4, ii) ammonia, iii) bromine and alkali. Statement II: p-toluidine can be converted into 3,5-dibromotoluene using reagents (i) Br2-H2O, (ii) NaNO2/HCl (0-5°C), (iii) aq. H3PO2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution: Statement I: KMnO4/H+ oxidizes side chains to carboxylic acids, converted to amide via NH3, then Hofmann bromamide (Br2+KOH) gives the diamine — correct sequence. Statement II: Bromination directs ortho to NH2, diazotization then H3PO2 replaces the original amino group with H, leaving the dibromo product — correct sequence.

questions.question: A student is given compound 'x' of molecular formula C6H7N. 'x' is sparingly soluble in water but becomes soluble with dilute mineral acid. 'x' with CHCl3 and KOH(alc.) gives 'y' with unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, 'x' gives compound 'z' soluble in alkali. The number of different H atoms present in 'z' is:
questions.solution: x is aniline (C6H5NH2). Carbylamine reaction with CHCl3/KOH gives phenyl isocyanide (y, unpleasant smell). Hinsberg test with benzenesulphonyl chloride gives N-phenylbenzenesulfonamide (z, soluble in alkali since it's a secondary sulfonamide from a primary amine). Counting distinct H environments in Ph-NH-SO2-Ph gives 7 different types of H atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one-electron system?

options.1: -1.09×10⁻¹⁸ J for second orbit of H atom
options.2: +2.18×10⁻¹⁸ J for second orbit of He⁺ ion
options.3: +8.72×10⁻¹⁸ J for first orbit of He⁺ ion
options.4: -2.18×10⁻¹⁸ J for third orbit of Li²⁺ ion

questions.solution: En = -2.18×10⁻¹⁸ Z²/n² J/atom. For 3rd orbit of Li²⁺ (Z=3,n=3): En = -2.18×10⁻¹⁸ * 9/9 = -2.18×10⁻¹⁸ J.

questions.question: Which one of the following graphs accurately represents the plot of partial pressure of CS2 vs its mole fraction in a mixture of acetone and CS2 at constant temperature?

options.1: Graph showing positive deviation with Henry's/Raoult's law lines

questions.solution: Mixture of CS2 and acetone shows positive deviation from Raoult's law, so PCS2 > P°CS2 * XCS2, matching graph option (1).

questions.question: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the 3rd period of periodic table is:
questions.solution: In general ionization energy increases left to right due to increasing Zeff, with an anomaly at P (half-filled stable configuration gives higher IE than S): Al < Si < S < P < Cl.

questions.question: For the conversion of 2-bromo-1-methylbenzene derivative (X, with CH3 group) to a phenylacetic acid derivative (Y, with COOH), identify the correct sequence of reagents:
questions.solution: NaOEt eliminates HBr to form a vinyl/styrene derivative, then B2H6/H2O2 (hydroboration-oxidation, anti-Markovnikov) gives the primary alcohol, then Jones reagent oxidizes it to the carboxylic acid.

questions.question: In the electrochemical cell Ag(s)|AgCl(s)|FeCl2(aq),FeCl3(aq)|Pt(s) at 298K, the cell potential (Ecell) will increase when: (A) [Fe2+] increased (B) [Fe3+] decreased (C) [Fe2+] decreased (D) [Fe3+] increased (E) [Cl-] increased
questions.solution: Ecell = E°cell - (0.059/1)log([Fe2+]/([Cl-][Fe3+])). Ecell increases when [Fe2+] increases (A) or [Fe3+] decreases (B).

questions.question: 'x' is the product obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in presence of HCl followed by hydrolysis (Stephen reaction giving propanal). 'y' is obtained from but-2-ene by ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis (giving ethanal). From the following, which product is NOT obtained when one mole of x and one mole of y react in presence of alkali followed by heating (crossed aldol condensation)?
questions.solution: Propanal (X) has an alpha-CH3, ethanal (Y) has alpha-CH3. Crossed aldol/Claisen-Schmidt type condensation gives: 2-methylpent-2-enal, 2-methylbut-2-enal, and pent-2-enal, but NOT 3-methylbut-2-enal (that combination is not formed from these reactants).

questions.question: 4-Nitrotoluene undergoes: (i) Sn,HCl/Δ (ii) pH neutralisation → (A); then (i)(CH3CO)2O (ii)Br2/AcOH → (B). Assuming complete reaction, 137 mg of 4-nitrotoluene will produce ____ mg of B. (Molar mass: H=1,C=12,N=14,O=16,Br=80)
questions.solution: 4-nitrotoluene (MW=137) → reduction to 4-methylaniline (A) → acetylation then bromination gives brominated acetanilide derivative B (MW=228). Moles = 137×10⁻³/137 = 0.001 mol. Mass of B = 0.001×228 = 0.228 g = 228 mg.

questions.question: A cup of water at 5°C (system) is placed in a microwave oven and the oven is turned on for one minute during which the water begins to boil. Which of the following is true?
questions.solution: Heat is given to the system so q=+ve. Due to expansion of the system (water to steam), work is done by system so w=-ve. Internal energy increases (liquid to gas), so ΔU=+ve.

questions.question: Statement I: [CoBr4]²⁻ ion will absorb light of lower energy than [CoCl4]²⁻ ion. Statement II: In [CoI4]²⁻ ion, the energy separation between the two sets of d-orbitals is more than [CoCl4]²⁻ ion.

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.2: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: Statement I true: ligand strength Cl⁻>Br⁻, so Δt for CoCl4²⁻ > CoBr4²⁻, meaning CoBr4²⁻ absorbs lower energy light. Statement II false: ligand strength I⁻<Cl⁻, so Δt for CoI4²⁻ < CoCl4²⁻, not more.

questions.question: But-2-yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq.NH3 to give products X and Y respectively. Identify the incorrect statements: A. X and Y are stereoisomers. B. Dipole moment of X is zero. C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y. D. X and Y react with O3/Zn+H2O to give different products.
questions.solution: X (cis-but-2-ene, from Pd/C) has non-zero dipole moment, so B is incorrect (incorrect statement). Both X and Y give the same product (2CH3CHO/acetaldehyde) on ozonolysis regardless of cis/trans, so D is also incorrect. Correct incorrect-statements: B and D.

questions.question: Given: (A) n=5, ml=-1; (B) n=3,l=2,ml=-1,ms=+1/2. The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) respectively are:
questions.solution: (A) n=5: summing over allowed l values (0 to 4) where ml=-1 is possible gives total 8 electrons (2 electrons per valid l from l=1 to l=4). (B) Fully specified quantum numbers including ms allow only 1 electron.

questions.question: Consider compounds: a) chlorobenzene, b) nitrobenzene, c) anisole (methoxybenzene). Arrange in increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
questions.solution: -OMe is a strong electron donor (+M), activating the ring most; -NO2 is a strong electron withdrawer (-M), deactivating the ring most; -Cl is a weak deactivator (withdraws by induction but donates by resonance, milder deactivator than NO2). Increasing reactivity: NO2(b) < Cl(a) < OMe(c).

questions.question: The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are: A. It is red in colour. B. It has high solubility in water at pH=9. C. The Ni ion has two unpaired d-electrons. D. The N-Ni-N bond angle is almost close to 90°. E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles.
questions.solution: The complex Ni(dmgH)2 is rosy-red (A true), precipitated (insoluble) in basic medium (B is false/incorrect), Ni2+ is d8 square planar with dsp2 hybridization and 0 unpaired electrons (C is incorrect), N-Ni-N bond angle close to 90° in square planar geometry (D true), and it contains only two five-membered metallacycles, not four (E is incorrect). Incorrect statements: B, C, E.

questions.question: From the given cyclic structures (A to D), those which will NOT react with Tollen's reagent are:
questions.solution: Structures B and C are drawn as acetals/glycosides (no free anomeric -OH), hence they cannot form the open-chain aldehyde form and do not reduce Tollen's reagent.

questions.question: Identify the molecule (X) with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons (via Lewis dot structure) among HNO3, H2SO4, NF3 and O3. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of molecule (X).
questions.solution: NF3 has the maximum lone pairs (10 total including on F atoms) with sp3 hybridized N. Bond angle in NF3 ≈ 102° (compressed from 109.5° due to lone pair repulsion).

questions.question: Match List-I (Functional group detection) with List-II (Change observed): A. Unsaturation (Baeyer's test); B. Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test); C. Aldehyde group (Tollen's reagent); D. Phenolic group (FeCl3 test). List-II: I. Red colour appears; II. Silver mirror appears; III. Violet colour appears; IV. Discharge of pink colour.
questions.solution: A (Baeyer's test/unsaturation) discharges pink colour (IV). B (ceric ammonium nitrate for alcohols) gives red colour (I). C (Tollen's test for aldehydes) gives silver mirror (II). D (FeCl3 test for phenols) gives violet colour (III).

questions.question: Statement-I: Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point. Statement-II: The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced.

options.1: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
options.2: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
options.3: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
options.4: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false

questions.solution: Statement-I is false: sublimation is used for compounds that sublime (solid to vapor directly), not simply low melting point compounds. Statement-II is false: boiling point decreases as external pressure is reduced (not increases). Both statements are false.

questions.question: Compound 'P' undergoes: (i) NH3 (ii) Δ → Q; then (i) KOH,Br2 (ii) CHCl3, KOH(alc),Δ → a nitrile-substituted cyclohexane product. 'P' is:
questions.solution: Cyclohexanecarboxylic acid (P) reacts with NH3 then heat (Δ) to form the amide (Q, cyclohexanecarboxamide). This then undergoes Hofmann bromamide degradation (KOH, Br2) to form cyclohexylamine, which via carbylamine reaction (CHCl3, KOH(alc), Δ) forms the isocyanide (nitrile-like NC group) product.

questions.question: The correct statements from the following are: (A) Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group. (B) Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group. (C) Among group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy. (D) The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.
questions.solution: (A) is false: ionic radii of M3+ actually generally increases down the group (B3+<Al3+<Ga3+<In3+<Tl3+), so this trend as stated (decreases) is false — actually verified true order is increasing, so A as 'decreases' is false. (B) is false: electronegativity order is B>Tl>In>Ga>Al, not monotonically decreasing. (C) true: B has the highest IE among group 13 (B>Tl>Ga>Al>In). (D) true: trichlorides/triiodides of group 13 elements are covalent. Correct: C and D only.

questions.question: Consider the general reaction xA(g) ⇌ yB(g) at 400K. Kp and Kc studied under same T but variation in x,y: (i) Kp=85.87, Kc=2.586 (appropriate units); (ii) Kp=0.862, Kc=28.62 (appropriate units). The value of x and y in (i) and (ii) respectively are:
questions.solution: For reaction (i): Kp>Kc implies Δng>0, i.e., y>x. Solving 85.87=2.586(0.0821*400)^(y-x) gives y-x≈1, consistent with (i) x=1,y=2. For reaction (ii): Kp<Kc implies y<x, consistent with (ii) x=2,y=1.

questions.question: For the thermal decomposition of reaction AB(g), a graph of [AB] vs time is constructed (zero order, [AB] decreases from 0.60M at t=0 to 0.55M at t=100s, linear). The half life of the reaction is 'x' min.

For the gas phase equilibrium NH3(g) ⇌ (1/2)N2(g) + (3/2)H2(g) at constant temperature, if total pressure is √3 atm and Kp=9 atm, the degree of dissociation is given as (x×10⁻²)⁻¹/². The value of x is ____ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: Setting up Kp expression with degree of dissociation α and total pressure √3 atm: 9 = 9(α/2)²/(1-α²) leads to α²=0.8, α=(0.8)^(1/2)=[1/0.8]^(-1/2)=[125×10⁻²]^(-1/2). So x=125.

questions.question: x mg of pure HCl was used to make an aqueous solution. 25.0 mL of 0.1M Ba(OH)2 solution is used when the HCl solution is titrated against it. The numerical value of x is ____ ×10⁻¹. (Molar mass: HCl=36.5, Ba(OH)2=171.0 g/mol)
questions.solution: Ba(OH)2 + 2HCl → BaCl2 + 2H2O. Moles Ba(OH)2 = 25×0.1/1000=2.5 mmol, so HCl=5 mmol. Mass HCl = 5×36.5=182.5 mg = 1825×10⁻¹ mg. x=1825.

questions.question: Consider all structural isomers with molecular formula C5H11Br separately treated with KOH(aq) to give respective substitution products (SN2, no rearrangement). The number of products which can exhibit optical isomerism is ____.
questions.solution: Among the C5H11Br isomers, three of the resulting alcohol products (from isomers with a stereocenter) show optical isomerism (or 6 if counting both enantiomers of each as separate active isomers).

questions.question: The crystal field splitting energy of [Co(oxalate)3]³⁻ complex is 'n' times that of the [Cr(oxalate)3]³⁻ complex. Here 'n' is ____. (Assume Δ0 >> P)
questions.solution: Neglecting pairing energy relative to Δ0: [Co(ox)3]3- is Co3+ (d6, low spin, t2g^6) CFSE=6*(-0.4Δ0)=-2.4Δ0. [Cr(ox)3]3- is Cr3+ (d3, t2g^3) CFSE=3*(-0.4Δ0)=-1.2Δ0. Ratio CFSE(Co3+)/CFSE(Cr3+) = 2.4/1.2 = 2.

questions.question: Statement-I: Hybridisation, shape and spin only magnetic moment of K3[Co(CO3)3] is sp3d2, octahedral and 4.9 BM respectively. Statement-II: Geometry, hybridisation and spin only magnetic moment (BM) of [Ni(CN)4]2-,[MnBr4]2- and [CoF6]3- respectively are square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral: dsp2,sp3,sp3d2 and 0, 5.9, 4.9.

options.1: Both statement-I and II are false
options.2: Statement I is false but II is true
options.3: Both statement-I and II are true
options.4: Statement-I is true but II is false

questions.solution: In K3[Co(CO3)3]: sp3d2 hybridized, octahedral, 4 unpaired electrons, 4.9 BM (Statement I true). [Ni(CN)4]2-: dsp2, square planar, 0 unpaired electrons, 0 BM. [MnBr4]2-: sp3, tetrahedral, 5 unpaired electrons, 5.9 BM. [CoF6]3-: sp3d2, octahedral, 4 unpaired electrons, 4.9 BM (Statement II true). Both statements are true.

questions.question: A→D is an endothermic reaction occurring in three elementary steps: (i) A→B, ΔHi=+ve; (ii) B→C, ΔHii=-ve; (iii) C→D, ΔHiii=-ve. Which graph of potential energy vs reaction coordinate correctly represents A→D?
questions.solution: Since A→D is overall endothermic, ED>EA. Step-wise: A→B (EB>EA), B→C (EC<EB), C→D (ED<EC), with net ED>EA. This matches the profile with three humps of decreasing height, ending above the starting point A.

questions.question: Arrange the following alkenes in decreasing order of stability: I (tetrasubstituted), II (trans-disubstituted), III (trisubstituted), IV (cis-disubstituted)
questions.solution: Stability order based on degree of substitution and alpha-hydrogen count (hyperconjugation): tetrasubstituted (αH=12) > trisubstituted (αH=9) > trans-disubstituted (αH=6) > cis-disubstituted (αH=6), with trans more stable than cis. Order: I > III > II > IV.

questions.question: Given statements: A. Dipole moment of NF3 is higher than NH3. B. Dipole moment of BeH2 is zero. C. Bond order of O2^2- and F2 is same. D. Formal charge on central oxygen of ozone is -1. E. In NO2, all three atoms satisfy octet rule.
questions.solution: A is false: dipole moment NF3<NH3 (due to opposing lone pair and bond dipole directions in NF3). B is true: BeH2 is linear sp hybridized with zero dipole moment. C is true: both O2^2- and F2 have bond order 1. D is false: formal charge on central O in ozone is +1, not -1. E is false: N in NO2 doesn't follow octet rule (odd electron molecule). Correct: B & C only.

questions.question: A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.3g of nonvolatile nonelectrolyte solute A (M=60 g/mol) and 0.9g of nonvolatile nonelectrolyte solute B (M=180 g/mol) in 100mL H2O at 27°C. Osmotic pressure will be [R=0.082 L.atm/K.mol]
Among the following, the correct combinations are: A. IF3 → T-shaped (sp3d), B. IF5 → Square pyramidal (sp3d2), C. IF7 → Pentagonal bipyramidal (spd3), D. ClO4⁻ → Square planar (sp2d)
questions.solution: IF3 is T-shaped with sp3d hybridization (correct). IF5 is square pyramidal with sp3d2 hybridization (correct). IF7 is pentagonal bipyramidal with sp3d3 hybridization (correct, though labeled spd3 which likely means sp3d3). ClO4⁻ is actually tetrahedral with sp3 hybridization, not square planar (incorrect). So A, B, C only.

questions.question: The correct stability order of the following diazonium salts (with para substituents OCH3, NO2, H, CN) is?
questions.solution: Electron donating groups (+M, like OCH3) increase stability of the diazonium salt by donating into the ring, while electron withdrawing groups (-M, like NO2, CN) decrease stability. Order: A(OCH3) > C(H) > D(CN) > B(NO2).

questions.question: A mixture X is made by dissolving 0.4 mol of [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br and 0.4 mol of [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 in water to make 4L solution. 2L of X reacts with excess AgNO3 to form precipitate Y. The other 2L reacts with excess BaCl2 to form precipitate Z. Which statement is correct?

options.2: Y is BaSO4 and Z is AgBr

questions.solution: 2L of mixture contains 0.2 mol of each complex. With excess AgNO3, 0.2 mol AgBr (Y) forms (only from the ionizable Br⁻ in [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4, since Br is coordinated/complexed in the other). With excess BaCl2, 0.2 mol BaSO4 (Z) forms similarly. So 0.2 mol of Z is formed.

questions.question: Statement-I: The number of paramagnetic species among [CoF6]3-, [TiF6]3-, V2O5 and [Fe(CN)6]3- is 3. Statement-II: K4[Fe(CN)6]<K3[Fe(CN)6]<[Fe(H2O)6]SO4.H2O<[Fe(H2O)6]Cl3 is the correct order in terms of number of unpaired electrons.

options.1: Both statement-I and II are true
options.2: Both statement-I and II are false
options.3: Statement-I is true but II is false
options.4: Statement-I is false but II is true

questions.solution: Paramagnetic species: [CoF6]3-, [TiF6]3-, [Fe(CN)6]3- (3 species); V2O5 is diamagnetic. Statement I is true. questions.question: Consider three metal chlorides x,y,z, where x is water soluble at room temp, y is sparingly soluble in water at room temp, z is soluble in hot water. x,y,z are respectively
questions.solution: MgCl2, AlCl3, CuCl2 are all water soluble at room temperature. AgCl and Hg2Cl2 are sparingly soluble in water at room temperature. PbCl2 is soluble in hot water (but not cold water). So x=CuCl2, y=AgCl, z=PbCl2.

questions.question: Match List-I (Chloro derivative) with List-II (Example): A. Vinyl Chloride, B. Benzyl chloride, C. Alkyl chloride, D. Allyl chloride. List-II: I. CH2=CH-CH2Cl, II. CH3-CHCl-CH3, III. CH2=CHCl, IV. Ph-CHCl-CH3
questions.solution: Vinyl chloride is CH2=CHCl (III). Benzyl chloride is Ph-CH2Cl type structure (IV, shown as substituted variant). Alkyl chloride example is CH3-CHCl-CH3 (II). Allyl chloride is CH2=CH-CH2Cl (I). Match: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Match List-I (Isothermal process for ideal gas) with List-II (Work done if Vf>Vi): A. Reversible expansion, B. Free expansion, C. Irreversible expansion, D. Irreversible compression. List-II: I. w=0, II. w=-nRTln(Vf/Vi), III. w=-Pex(Vf-Vi), IV. w=-Pex(Vi-Vf)
questions.solution: Reversible expansion work: w=-nRTln(Vf/Vi) (II). Free expansion: Pext=0, so w=0 (I). Irreversible expansion: w=-Pext(Vf-Vi) (III). Irreversible compression: w=-Pext(Vi-Vf) (IV). Match: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.question: A student is given one compound among four cyclic structures (hemiacetal/acetal forms) that gives positive test with Tollen's reagent. The compound is:
questions.solution: The compound C is a hemiacetal (has free anomeric -OH), which can open to the free aldehyde form under basic conditions and give a positive Tollen's test (silver mirror), unlike the fully acetalized forms A and B which lack a free anomeric center.

questions.question: A hydroxy compound (X) with molar mass 122 g/mol is acetylated with acetic anhydride using excess reagent for complete acetylation. The product has molar mass 290 g/mol. The number of hydroxyl groups in X is:
questions.solution: Each OH→OCOCH3 conversion adds 42 g/mol (mass of acetyl group minus H). Number of OH groups=(290-122)/42=4.

questions.solution: x=H2 gas (from phenol+Na, molar mass 2). y=CO2 gas (from carboxylic acid+NaHCO3, molar mass 44). Sum=2+44=46.

questions.question: Arrange the following carbanions (with para substituents Br, H(phenyl), OCH3, CHO, CH3) in decreasing order of stability
questions.solution: Electron withdrawing groups (like -CHO) increase carbanion stability through resonance/induction, while electron donating groups (like -OCH3, -CH3) decrease stability. Order: IV(CHO) > I(Br) > II(H) > V(CH3) > III(OCH3).

questions.question: Statement I: K>Mg>Al>B is the correct order in terms of metallic character. Statement II: Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element.

options.1: Both Statement I and II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and II are false
options.3: Statement I is false but II is true
options.4: Statement I is true but II is false

questions.solution: Statement I is true: metallic character decreases across period/increases down group appropriately for these elements. Statement II is false: while cationic radius is always smaller than atomic radius, anionic radius is larger than atomic radius, so the statement 'always greater' is false in general.

questions.question: Electricity is passed through an acidic solution of Cu2+ till all Cu2+ was exhausted, depositing 300mg Cu. A current of 600mA was continued for another 28 minutes, keeping total volume at 200mL. The total volume of oxygen evolved at STP during the entire process is ____ mL. (Molar mass Cu=63.54, O2=32, F=96500, molar volume STP=22.4L)
questions.solution: Eq of Cu=Eq of O2 initially: (300×10⁻³×2)/63.54=nO2×4, giving nO2=2.36×10⁻³ mol. From further current: nO2×4=(600×28×60)/(96500×1000), giving nO2=2.611×10⁻³ mol. Total O2=10⁻³×(2.36+2.611)×22400=111.35 mL≈111.

questions.question: Consider two Group IV metal ions X2+ and Y2+. A solution containing 0.01M X2+ and 0.01M Y2+ is saturated with H2S. The pH at which metal sulphide YS will form as precipitate is ____ (Ksp(XS)=1×10⁻²², Ksp(YS)=4×10⁻¹⁶, [H2S]=0.1M, Ka1×Ka2=1.0×10⁻²¹, log2=0.30,log3=0.48,log5=0.70)
questions.solution: For YS precipitation: [S2-]≥Ksp(YS)/[Y2+]=4×10⁻¹⁶/10⁻²=4×10⁻¹⁴. Using [S2-]=Ka1Ka2[H2S]/[H+]²≥4×10⁻¹⁴, solving gives [H+]≤(1/2)×10⁻⁴, so pH≥4.3, nearest integer 4.
